scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify that the hero section displays correctly with product name, tagline, animated logo, and call-to-action buttons

steps.description: Navigate to the homepage URL
steps.context: User visits the MirDB product homepage for the first time

steps.description: Check that product name 'MirDB' is displayed prominently, tagline 'A Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol' is visible, and animated logo GIF loads correctly
steps.context: Hero section should be the first visible content above the fold

steps.description: Check that primary CTA 'Get Started' or 'View on GitHub' and secondary CTA 'Read Documentation' are present and clickable
steps.context: CTAs should guide users to take action

test_cases.expected: Hero section is visible with product name 'MirDB' as h1 heading
Tagline text contains 'Persistent Key-Value Store' and 'Memcached'
Logo image element exists with src pointing to assets/logo.gif and appropriate alt text
Button navigates to GitHub repository or documentation section
Secondary CTA for documentation is visible and functional

scenarios.name: Features Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify that all key features are displayed in a grid/card layout with appropriate icons and descriptions

steps.description: Navigate to the features section of the homepage
steps.context: Features section appears after the hero section

steps.description: Check that all 5 key features are displayed: Memcached Protocol, Skip-list Memtable, Compaction, Tokio Async Runtime, Persistent Storage
steps.context: Each feature should have an icon, title, and brief description

test_cases.input: Count feature cards/items in features section
test_cases.expected: At least 5 feature cards are present
Feature card with 'Memcached Protocol' title and description about compatibility exists
Feature card with 'Skip-list' or 'Memtable' title and description about in-memory efficiency exists
Feature card mentioning 'Compaction' with description about storage optimization exists
Feature card mentioning 'Tokio' or 'Async' with performance description exists
Feature card mentioning 'Persistent' or 'LSM-tree' with durability description exists

test_cases.input: Verify feature grid layout on desktop
test_cases.expected: Features are displayed in a grid layout (not stacked vertically) on desktop viewport

scenarios.name: Code Example Section
scenarios.description: Verify that the code example section displays syntax-highlighted code with copy-to-clipboard functionality

steps.description: Find the section displaying usage code examples
steps.context: Code example demonstrates how easy it is to use MirDB

steps.description: Check that code is properly syntax-highlighted using Prism.js or similar library
steps.context: Highlighting should make code readable and professional

steps.description: Click copy button and verify code is copied to clipboard
steps.context: Users should be able to easily copy code examples

test_cases.expected: Pre/code element exists with example code content
Code example shows GET/SET operations or connection examples
Code elements have Prism.js or highlight.js classes applied
Code content is copied to system clipboard, button shows success feedback
Copy button is visible near or within the code block

scenarios.name: Quick Start Installation Section
scenarios.description: Verify that quick-start instructions are clear, complete, and properly formatted

steps.description: Find the installation/getting started section
steps.context: New users need clear installation instructions

steps.description: Check that cargo/build commands and configuration basics are provided
steps.context: Instructions should be step-by-step and easy to follow

test_cases.expected: Section with 'Quick Start', 'Getting Started', or 'Installation' heading exists
Installation instructions include cargo build or cargo install commands
Instructions are presented as numbered steps or clear sequential process
Basic configuration options or default settings are mentioned

scenarios.name: GitHub Integration and Status Badges
scenarios.description: Verify that GitHub repository link is prominent and CI status badge is displayed

steps.description: Find the prominent link to the GitHub repository
steps.context: GitHub link should be easily accessible from multiple locations

steps.description: Check that CircleCI build status badge is displayed
steps.context: Badge shows project health and build status

test_cases.input: Check for GitHub link in hero section
test_cases.expected: Link to github.com/yetone/mirdb exists in hero or header area
GitHub link has correct href attribute pointing to repository
CircleCI badge image is present and loads correctly

test_cases.input: Verify badge links to CI dashboard
test_cases.expected: Clicking badge navigates to CircleCI build page

test_cases.input: Check for GitHub link in footer
test_cases.expected: Footer contains link to GitHub repository

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Mobile
scenarios.description: Verify that the homepage is fully responsive and displays correctly on mobile devices

steps.description: View the homepage at mobile viewport width (375px or less)
steps.context: Mobile users should have a good experience

steps.description: Check that all text is readable without horizontal scrolling
steps.context: Content should reflow appropriately for small screens

steps.description: Verify all buttons and links are tappable with appropriate touch targets
steps.context: Touch targets should be at least 44x44 pixels

test_cases.expected: No horizontal scroll bar appears, content fits within viewport
Hero content stacks vertically and remains readable
Feature cards stack vertically in single column layout

test_cases.input: Verify CTA button size on mobile
test_cases.expected: CTA buttons have minimum touch target size of 44x44 pixels
Code block is scrollable horizontally if needed, or wraps appropriately

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Tablet
scenarios.description: Verify that the homepage displays correctly on tablet devices

steps.description: View the homepage at tablet viewport width (768px)
steps.context: Tablet users should have an optimized experience

steps.description: Check that layout adapts appropriately between mobile and desktop
steps.context: Tablet layout may use 2-column grids

test_cases.expected: Layout adapts to tablet viewport without horizontal overflow
Features display in 2-column or adapted grid layout
Hero content is proportionally sized for tablet viewport

scenarios.name: Accessibility Compliance
scenarios.description: Verify that the homepage meets WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards

steps.description: Use automated tools to check WCAG compliance
steps.context: Accessibility is a must-have requirement

steps.description: Navigate through all interactive elements using only keyboard
steps.context: Users who cannot use a mouse must be able to navigate

steps.description: Check that semantic HTML and ARIA labels are properly implemented
steps.context: Screen reader users need proper page structure

test_cases.expected: Document has proper heading hierarchy (h1, h2, h3) without skipping levels

test_cases.input: Verify all images have alt text
test_cases.expected: All img elements have meaningful alt attributes
All interactive elements are reachable via Tab key in logical order
Text has minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio against backgrounds (AA standard)
Interactive elements have visible focus indicators when focused
Links have descriptive text (no 'click here' or 'read more' without context)
Page uses semantic elements (header, main, nav, footer, section, article)

scenarios.name: Performance and Load Time
scenarios.description: Verify that the page meets performance requirements including load time under 3 seconds

steps.description: Test page load time on simulated 3G connection
steps.context: NFR-2 requires load time < 3 seconds on 3G

steps.description: Execute Lighthouse performance audit and verify score > 90
steps.context: Success criteria requires Lighthouse score > 90

steps.description: Check that images and GIFs are optimized for web delivery
steps.context: Large assets should not block rendering

test_cases.input: Measure page load time on 3G throttling
test_cases.expected: Page fully loads within 3 seconds on 3G connection
Lighthouse performance score is 90 or higher
GIF and image assets are reasonably optimized (logo.gif and usage.gif)
Main CSS file is under 50KB uncompressed
Main JS file is under 50KB uncompressed (excluding Prism.js library)
No critical render-blocking resources that delay first paint significantly

scenarios.name: Cross-Browser Compatibility
scenarios.description: Verify that the homepage renders correctly across all major browsers

steps.description: Verify full functionality on Google Chrome
steps.context: Chrome is the most widely used browser

steps.description: Verify full functionality on Mozilla Firefox
steps.context: Firefox has different rendering engine (Gecko)

steps.description: Verify full functionality on Safari
steps.context: Safari uses WebKit and is important for Mac/iOS users

steps.description: Verify full functionality on Microsoft Edge
steps.context: Edge is the default Windows browser

test_cases.input: Load page in Chrome latest version
test_cases.expected: All sections render correctly, no layout issues, all functionality works

test_cases.input: Load page in Firefox latest version
test_cases.expected: All sections render correctly, no layout issues, all functionality works

test_cases.input: Load page in Safari latest version
test_cases.expected: All sections render correctly, no layout issues, all functionality works

test_cases.input: Load page in Edge latest version
test_cases.expected: All sections render correctly, no layout issues, all functionality works
CSS variables are properly applied across all browsers

scenarios.name: Dark/Light Mode Theming
scenarios.description: Verify that the page supports dark and light mode theming

steps.description: Verify page loads with appropriate default theme
steps.context: Page should respect system preferences or have sensible default

steps.description: Toggle between dark and light mode and verify all elements adapt
steps.context: All text, backgrounds, and UI elements should change appropriately

steps.description: Verify page responds to prefers-color-scheme media query
steps.context: Users with system-wide dark mode should see dark theme by default

test_cases.input: Check for CSS custom properties for theming
test_cases.expected: CSS variables defined for colors that change between themes
Page displays dark theme with appropriate dark backgrounds and light text
Page displays light theme with appropriate light backgrounds and dark text
Code syntax highlighting adapts to current theme
Text maintains readable contrast against dark backgrounds

scenarios.name: SEO and Meta Tags
scenarios.description: Verify that the page has proper SEO optimization and meta tags

steps.description: Verify presence of essential meta tags for SEO
steps.context: Meta tags improve search engine discoverability

steps.description: Check for social sharing meta tags
steps.context: OG tags improve appearance when shared on social media

test_cases.expected: Document has title tag containing 'MirDB' and relevant keywords
Meta description tag exists with compelling description under 160 characters
Viewport meta tag is present for responsive design
OG title, description, and image tags are present
Canonical link tag points to the primary URL
Twitter card meta tags are present for rich sharing

scenarios.name: Footer Section
scenarios.description: Verify that the footer contains required information and links

steps.description: Navigate to the page footer
steps.context: Footer should be at the bottom of the page

steps.description: Check for GitHub link, license info, and CI badge
steps.context: Footer provides important project information

test_cases.expected: Semantic footer element exists at bottom of page
Footer contains link to GitHub repository
Footer displays license type or links to license
Footer is visible when scrolled to bottom of page

scenarios.name: Navigation and Documentation Links
scenarios.description: Verify that navigation to documentation sections works correctly

steps.description: Identify navigation links to documentation sections
steps.context: Users need easy access to documentation

steps.description: Click navigation links and verify they navigate correctly
steps.context: Links may be anchor links or external documentation

test_cases.input: Check for navigation element or links
test_cases.expected: Navigation links to different sections or documentation exist
Clicking section links scrolls to appropriate section smoothly
Read Documentation button navigates to docs or appropriate section

scenarios.name: Usage GIF Display
scenarios.description: Verify that the usage demonstration GIF loads and displays correctly

steps.description: Find the section displaying the usage GIF from /assets/usage.gif
steps.context: Visual demonstration helps users understand the product

steps.description: Check that GIF loads, animates, and has appropriate alt text
steps.context: GIF should show how easy MirDB is to use

test_cases.expected: Image element with src pointing to assets/usage.gif exists

test_cases.input: Verify usage GIF has alt text
test_cases.expected: Usage GIF has descriptive alt text for accessibility

test_cases.input: Check usage GIF loads without error
test_cases.expected: GIF file loads successfully without 404 or network errors

test_cases.input: Verify GIF is visible in viewport
test_cases.expected: Usage demonstration is visible when scrolling through page

scenarios.name: Static File Structure Validation
scenarios.description: Verify that the static site file structure is correct and all files exist

steps.description: Check that index.html, styles/main.css, and scripts/main.js exist
steps.context: Proper file structure is essential for deployment

steps.description: Ensure HTML is valid and well-formed
steps.context: Valid HTML prevents rendering issues

test_cases.expected: index.html exists in the homepage directory
styles/main.css or equivalent CSS file exists
scripts/main.js or equivalent JS file exists
HTML passes W3C validation without critical errors
CSS file is properly linked in HTML head
JS file is properly linked, preferably at end of body or with defer
